byteward.sentence: A security flaw in Brightmesh home routers lets attackers take full control of them over the internet.
The flaw affects 11 router models in the company's BX series.
Brightmesh released firmware version 4.2.1 on Wednesday to fix it.
Researchers at the security firm Quillstone found the flaw.
Routers set to update automatically will install the fix within 48 hours.

launch-desk.sentence: Firmware 4.2.1, out now, closes the hole.
Three older models won't get the fix.
Brightmesh says it will replace those routers for free.
Brightmesh shares fell 6% in early trading.

frametime.sentence: Brightmesh has patched a flaw that let attackers take over its home routers.
The update took 6 minutes to install, including a restart.
Download speeds dropped 3% after the update in our testing.
Latency in online games went from 14 ms to 15 ms.

ohm-and-bit.sentence: Brightmesh has fixed a flaw that let attackers seize control of its home routers.
Eleven models in the BX series are affected.
The bug sits in the routers' remote management service, the part that answers requests from the internet.
Along with the fix, the update switches remote management off by default.
Three older BX models won't be patched.
They don't have enough storage to hold the new firmware.

bench-and-bill.sentence: Brightmesh has released a fix in firmware 4.2.1.
On Wednesday, the National Cyber Readiness Office ordered federal agencies to patch or unplug any affected Brightmesh routers on their networks.
Agencies have until November 25 to comply.
The office says attackers are already exploiting the flaw.
